raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

The Elastic EP Scaling test (distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling) failed with AITER on. The cause is:
1. AITER requires a torch.distributed-registered group, but Elastic EP is using stateless group, which is not torch.distributed registered at all, so we need to skip AITER AR and choose next available AR;
2. During scale-up, existing workers call _release_cuda_graphs() and then re-capture into the same global graph pool. Some memory in that pool was still allocated, because FlyDSL didn't release them correctly. Graph replay never re-enters Python, so a kernel last launched during capture holds those tensors inside the graph pool indefinitely. The pool had no graphs left but still had live blocks, so PyTorch rejected capturing into it again. Now I explicitly call _switch_to_fresh_graph_pool() to switch to a new graph pool to avoid this.

## Claims

These 2 bugs are fixed. This test case works as expected no matter AITER is on or off.

@@ -165,9 +165,15 @@ def __init__(
                 register_graph_buffers=register,
             )
 
-        # AITER custom all-gather/reduce-scatter DP-attention dispatch/combine
+        # AITER custom all-gather/reduce-scatter DP-attention dispatch/combine.
+        # AITER requires a torch.distributed-registered group and exchanges IPC
+        # handles via the default store; stateless groups satisfy neither.
+        # Only StatelessGroupCoordinator passes tcp_store_group, so this checks
+        # the property AITER depends on rather than the feature that currently
+        # creates stateless groups (elastic EP).
         if (
             "dp" in unique_name
+            and tcp_store_group is None
             and self.world_size in (2, 4, 8)
             and current_platform.is_rocm()
             and rocm_aiter_ops.is_custom_all_reduce_enabled()

@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@
 import torch.nn as nn
 from torch.distributed import P2POp
 
+from vllm.compilation.breakable_cudagraph import BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper
 from vllm.compilation.cuda_graph import CUDAGraphWrapper
 from vllm.compilation.wrapper import reset_compile_wrapper
 from vllm.config import ParallelConfig, set_current_vllm_config
@@ -460,6 +461,37 @@ def _release_cuda_graphs(self) -> None:
         gc.collect()
         torch.accelerator.synchronize()
         torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+        self._switch_to_fresh_graph_pool()
+
+    def _switch_to_fresh_graph_pool(self) -> None:
+        # Libraries may keep capture-time tensors alive after their graphs are
+        # released (e.g. FlyDSL retains the last launch's DLPack arguments), so
+        # the old pool cannot be erased. Re-capturing into that pool trips the
+        # allocator's "use_count > 0" assert; capture into a fresh one instead.
+        platform_cls = type(current_platform)
+        if platform_cls._global_graph_pool is None:
+            return
+        new_pool = current_platform.graph_pool_handle()
+        platform_cls._global_graph_pool = new_pool
+
+        model_runner = self.worker.model_runner
+        manager = getattr(model_runner, "cudagraph_manager", None)
+        speculator = getattr(model_runner, "speculator", None)
+        managers = [manager] + [
+            attr
+            for attr in (vars(speculator).values() if speculator else ())
+            if isinstance(attr, CudaGraphManager)
+        ]
+        for m in managers:
+            if m is not None and m.pool is not None:
+                m.pool = new_pool
+
+        wrappers: list[CUDAGraphWrapper | BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper] = [
+            *CUDAGraphWrapper._all_instances,
+            *BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper._all_instances,
+        ]
+        for wrapper in wrappers:
+            wrapper.graph_pool = new_pool
 
     def switch_and_remove(self) -> None:
         # Removing ranks skipped preparation, so wait for prior cleanup here.
